record.paper_title: Protocols for Observational Studies: Methods and Open Problems
record.original_question: In an observational study that uses an elaborate theory, meaning a prespecified set of multiple predictions about how the data should look if the treatment has an effect, what methods can assess the evidence for the elaborate theory when investigators may want both prioritized testing of some predictions and information about all aspects of the theory, including the fraction of the theory corroborated and the evidence for individual aspects?

evidence.quote: An elaborate theory is a set of multiple predictions about how the data would look if the treatment has an effect.
Thus, an elaborate theory and a plan to test it should be specified in the protocol.

Although ordered testing of an elaborate theory has considerable advantages, one negative aspect is that although one might want to put a higher priority on certain aspects of the theory, one might want some information on all aspects. A different approach to assessing the evidence for an elaborate theory is to make inferences about the fraction of the elaborate theory that is corroborated as well as individual aspects of the theory [65]. Further research on ways to assess the evidence for an elaborate theory would be useful.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to combine prioritized (ordered) testing with inference on the fraction of an elaborate theory corroborated, while also reporting evidence on each individual prediction, is identified as an active research direction. Existing work develops prediction-based tests for multiple endpoints and quantitative inference about the amount of an elaborate theory supported, but a unified, fully satisfactory methodology meeting all three desiderata simultaneously does not appear to be established; the topic is still flagged as needing further research.

status_evidence.title: Testing an Elaborate Theory of a Causal Hypothesis - University of Washington
status_evidence.snippet: Statistical tests for the various pieces of the elaborate theory help to clarify how much the causal hypothesis is corroborated... a quantitative approach to making statistical inference about the amount of the elaborate theory supported by evidence.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative inference on the corroborated fraction of an elaborate theory is an active research direction, with verbal/ad hoc approaches still common.

status_evidence.title: A prediction-based test for multiple endpoints
status_evidence.snippet: Prediction-based tests combining multiple endpoints in observational studies of treatment effects.
status_evidence.claim: Methods for prediction-based testing of multiple endpoints exist but do not jointly resolve prioritization, individual inference, and corroborated-fraction inference.
